## Research question
Is Loamwise-ViT robust to JPEG compression of field photographs?

## Methods summary
Loamwise-ViT is a vision transformer for crop-disease diagnosis from leaf photographs that uses overlapping patch embeddings and a lesion-focused attention pooling head. Ferncastle-CNN, a convolutional classifier widely used in agricultural deployments, is the main baseline; Quillon-Mix, a hybrid convolution–attention model, is a second baseline.

## Experimental setup
All models are trained on the Harrowfield-Leaf training split (31,200 field photographs; 14 classes: 12 diseases, nutrient deficiency and healthy) with 5 seeds and evaluated by top-1 accuracy (%) on the 4,800-image test split; seed-level results are paired. Training images are stored losslessly and no compression, blur or brightness augmentation is used. Three perturbation families are applied to test images only: JPEG re-compression at quality settings 90, 70, 50, 30 and 10; motion blur with kernel lengths of 3, 7 and 11 pixels; and illumination change by scaling brightness to 0.8, 0.6 and 0.4 of the original. The project plan pre-specified the following criterion: a model counts as robust at a perturbation setting if its top-1 accuracy drops by at most 2.0 points from its clean test accuracy.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: Clean test accuracy
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Loamwise-ViT vs Ferncastle-CNN, top-1 accuracy, clean test split
  - comparison `exp1/cmp2`: Loamwise-ViT vs Quillon-Mix, top-1 accuracy, clean test split
- `exp2`: JPEG re-compression of test images
  - comparison `exp2/cmp3`: Accuracy drop from clean at each JPEG quality setting, Loamwise-ViT and Ferncastle-CNN
- `exp3`: Motion blur of test images
  - comparison `exp3/cmp4`: Accuracy drop from clean at each blur kernel length, Loamwise-ViT and Ferncastle-CNN
- `exp4`: Illumination change of test images
  - comparison `exp4/cmp5`: Accuracy drop from clean at each brightness scale, Loamwise-ViT and Ferncastle-CNN

## Statistical tests
- `S1` for comparison `exp1/cmp1`: paired t-test; two-sided; paired; n=5 random seeds; t=8.44 (df=4); p = 0.0011; 95% CI [1.14, 2.26] for mean paired difference in clean top-1 accuracy (Loamwise-ViT − Ferncastle-CNN), percentage points; alpha=0.05

## Cited source passages
- `P1` — Abernathy-Nkosi et al. (2022), "Harrowfield-Leaf: Field Photographs for Smallholder Crop-Disease Diagnosis":
  > Images were captured by extension officers with handheld phones across 41 smallholder farms over three growing seasons; each image was labelled by two plant pathologists, and disagreements (6.2% of images) were resolved by a third.
- `P2` — Ferreira-Lund & Watanabe (2021), "Motion Blur in Handheld Crop Imaging":
  > In our field survey, 23% of handheld leaf photographs showed visible motion blur, most often when images were taken in wind or from moving vehicles.
- `P3` — Dewhurst & Achebe-Lim (2020), "Ferncastle: Efficient Convolutional Networks for Plant Pathology":
  > Ferncastle-CNN uses depthwise-separable convolutions with squeeze-and-excitation blocks and is trained with random-resized crops, horizontal flips and colour jitter.

## Task
Write a short Results/Discussion passage (2–4 sentences) that answers the research question using only the evidence in this package.

sentences.text: Loamwise-ViT is robust to JPEG re-compression of test images at all evaluated quality settings (90, 70, 50, 30, 10), with mean accuracy drops of 0.1 to 1.8 points from clean, all within the pre-specified 2.0-point robustness criterion.
Under JPEG re-compression, Loamwise-ViT shows smaller mean accuracy drops than Ferncastle-CNN at every quality setting, with the gap widening at lower quality (e.g., 1.8 vs 9.8 points at quality 10).

Loamwise-ViT also shows smaller mean accuracy drops than Ferncastle-CNN under motion blur (kernel lengths 3, 7, 11 px) and illumination change (brightness ×0.8, ×0.6, ×0.4), but it exceeds the 2.0-point robustness criterion at the strongest blur (6.1 points at 11 px) and strongest illumination change (3.4 points at ×0.4).

On clean test images, Loamwise-ViT achieves higher top-1 accuracy (91.4 ± 0.4%) than Ferncastle-CNN (89.7 ± 0.4%), a statistically significant mean paired difference of 1.7 points (95% CI [1.14, 2.26], p = 0.0011).
